title: Rapid-response and recoverability play for Hosted API 5xx + timeout bursts
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: During a high-severity customer escalation on 2026-03-09 we observed repeated 5xx responses and client-facing timeouts for the Hosted API for ~2.5 hours. Impact was concentrated on a small set of high-throughput tenants using long-context generation. Multiple retrying clients amplified load and led to connection pool exhaustion and KV-cache churn, producing a feedback loop of tail latency and 502/504 errors. Scope: Hosted API frontend + serving runtime + auth/token rotation interactions. Multiple customers reported degraded SLOs and one enterprise customer opened an escalation with Support. Root cause (short): a synchronized token refresh and background cache purge triggered a burst of backend work that exhausted CUDA worker queues and the HTTP connection pool. Retries from clients (no jitter) and our aggressive per-request synchronous fallback logic caused request amplification and resource contention. Actions taken (incident response): 1) Immediate mitigation (10m): applied a global circuit-breaker to reject excess traffic for non-SLA tenants and increased per-worker HTTP connection pool size to reduce queued accept latency. 2) Retry dampening (30m): rolled forward a hotfix that adds jitter to internal retries, enforces an exponential-backoff cap, and limits concurrent per-tenant inflight requests. 3) Staggered auth refresh (1h): deployed a patch to stagger token refreshes across nodes to avoid synchronized spikes. 4) Serving fallback (1.5h): enabled a temporary fallback routing rule that sent 5% of traffic to a smaller, warmed model pool for long-context requests. 5) Observability & guardrails (incident window): added request_id propagation through the runtime, tightened SLO alert thresholds, and published a temporary dashboard for support to surface affected tenant IDs. Post-incident next steps: - Full postmortem with timeline and metric atlas (owner: Marcus Li, due 2026-03-18). - Permanent circuit-breaker and per-tenant concurrency limits as a platform feature (RFC planned). - Improve client SDK recommendations for retry jitter and backoff; add sample code and update docs. - Expand warm pool strategy and prewarming heuristics for long-context workloads. Technical notes: connection pool exhaustion symptoms were visible in Nginx error logs and runtime accept latency histograms; GPU queue length and KV cache eviction spikes correlated with increased 99.9th token latency. The token refresh service had an edge case that refreshed multiple tenants simultaneously when a Redis TTL expired. The fix staggers refresh by node and adds a small randomized delay. Outcome: customer escalations de-escalated after mitigations; error rate returned to baseline within ~2.5 hours. Hotfix PRs and rolling updates were successful with no rollback required. This ticket tracks the stabilization and productionization of the temporary mitigations.
